meta.description: Left-align and trim indels to parsimonious canonical form, decompose MNPs (atomize), and split multiallelic variants with bcftools norm. Use when comparing variants across callers or cohorts, preparing a VCF for database annotation or ClinVar/dbSNP matching, merging VCFs, reconciling vt-vs-bcftools representation discordance, or resolving the VCF-left-align vs HGVS-3'-rule clash.
meta.environment: bcftools 1.24 via WSL science/bio; cyvcf2 0.34.0 installed 2026-09-27 into a dedicated venv (audit-envs/bio-variant-normalization/venv, --system-site-packages) since the shared bio env only had numpy; vt still not installed (checked again, unchanged from prior audit).

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/trial results anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md; the one citation (Tan/Abecasis/Kang 2015) is a real, correctly described paper. All worked examples (chr1:506 AA>A -> chr1:500 GA>G, the 11L>11F consequence, the split/atomize record counts) were independently reproduced with bcftools 1.24 in this audit and matched.

practice_boundaries.detail: Scope stays at variant representation and matching; no diagnostic or prescriptive clinical conclusion is made anywhere, and clinical interpretation is explicitly deferred to variant-calling/clinical-interpretation.

methodological_ground.detail: No substituted-causation or mismatched-model fallacies found. The adversarial input (7) confirmed the skill does not silently endorse blind use of `-c s`: SKILL.md's caution ('REF mismatches often indicate a genome build mismatch, and silently fixing REF may mask a liftover error') sits directly next to the command and matches the observed silent-rewrite-with-exit-0 behavior.

code_usability.detail: All CLI/pipeline commands and both example scripts (normalize_vcf.sh, check_normalization.py) ran to completion without syntax errors or missing dependencies across all 7 inputs. One non-blocking robustness gap found in check_normalization.py (unhandled IndexError on missing argv) — code still runs correctly for its documented usage, so this is a P2 quality note, not an M4 failure.

functional_suitability.note: Covers left-align, split/join, atomize, dedup, REF-fixing, caller comparison, DB-annotation prep, GWAS prep, and the cyvcf2 pre-check, matching every use case in the frontmatter description; all verified correct against bcftools 1.24.

reliability.note: REF-mismatch preflight with pipefail rationale, a Common Errors table covering 8 distinct failure modes, and an empirically-verified idempotent normalization path. Category-3 override applied: hard-stop-on-mismatch is scored as correct defensive design, not a fault-tolerance defect.

performance_context.note: Post-fix layering is now clean: SKILL.md holds mechanics, usage-guide.md (61 lines) is onboarding-only and points back to SKILL.md/examples/, and the cyvcf2 script lives in its own file instead of inline. This directly fixes what would have been a low score pre-fix (397-line usage-guide.md re-stating SKILL.md).

agent_usability.note: Order-of-operations is explained with the failure mode it prevents (spurious ALT=* if atomized before split); Quick Reference and Common Errors tables give unambiguous feedback contracts.

human_usability.note: Description and usage-guide Example Prompts use natural researcher phrasing ('extra private variants', 'showing as absent'). Category-3 override applied to Forgiveness: strict REF-mismatch rejection is a data-integrity guarantee, not a usability defect, and the error message identifies the exact problem.

security.note: No credentials, no destructive operations, no injection vectors. Docked 1 point: examples/check_normalization.py does not validate argv before indexing it (confirmed: running it with no arguments raises a bare IndexError traceback instead of a usage message), unlike examples/normalize_vcf.sh which does check $#.

maintainability.note: Clean separation of concerns after the fix: decision logic (SKILL.md), onboarding (usage-guide.md), runnable code (examples/). Extracting the cyvcf2 block into its own file removed the only real coupling between prose and code that existed pre-fix.

agent_specific.note: Trigger description is specific (ClinVar/dbSNP matching, vt-vs-bcftools discordance, HGVS clash) without being narrow; SKILL.md is 408 lines with real supporting files actually used; Related Skills list gives clean composability; idempotence and escape-hatch guidance (when normalization is safe to skip, when NOT to use -c s blindly) are both explicit and were verified to hold in execution.

key_strengths: The usage-guide.md trim eliminated the near-total duplication of SKILL.md that the repo's FIX_BRIEF forbids (397 -> 61 lines), and a line-by-line diff against the pre-trim commit confirms every removed tip/caveat still lives, word-for-word or better, in SKILL.md.
examples/check_normalization.py produces output byte-identical to the pre-trim inline SKILL.md script on the same synthetic VCF -- the refactor changed packaging, not behavior.
Split-before-atomize ordering, the REF-mismatch preflight, idempotence, and the documented vt/bcftools atomization-equivalence workaround all still hold under fresh bcftools 1.24 regression testing.

The skill proactively documents genuinely load-bearing gotchas (Number=. field mis-subsetting, the VCF-left-align vs HGVS-3'-rule clash, bcftools csq's phase requirement) with concrete, independently-reproduced before/after evidence rather than generic caveats.

recommendations.title: check_normalization.py has no argv validation
recommendations.problem: Running `python examples/check_normalization.py` with no arguments raises an unhandled IndexError traceback instead of a usage message.
recommendations.root_cause: The script was extracted from an inline SKILL.md code block that assumed an agent would edit the hardcoded path in place; it was wrapped in main()/argv without adding the same $#-style guard that examples/normalize_vcf.sh already has.
recommendations.fix: Add an argument-count check at the top of __main__ (e.g. `if len(sys.argv) != 2: print('Usage: python check_normalization.py <input.vcf.gz>'); sys.exit(1)`), mirroring normalize_vcf.sh's existing pattern.
